content_units: Participants:   Product Manager, Designer, 2 Engineers, QA Lead
-   Final 10 minutes are reserved for decisions and next steps
Phase   Time   Goal   Key Tasks   Deliverable
Opening and priorities   09:30–09:35   Align on meeting outcomes   Confirm agenda; restate launch goal; flag any blockers needing priority   Shared priorities for the session
Beta bug triage   09:35–09:55   Review and rank beta issues   Review top bugs; assess severity and user impact; identify launch-critical fixes   Prioritized bug list
Onboarding drop-off metrics   09:55–10:10   Understand funnel issues   Review latest drop-off points; discuss likely causes; identify tests or UX fixes   Agreed metric insights and focus areas
Launch checklist review   10:10–10:25   Confirm launch readiness   Walk through checklist status; flag missing items; identify risks and dependencies   Updated launch readiness view
Owner assignments   10:25–10:35   Assign accountable owners   Match tasks to PM/design/engineering/QA; confirm deadlines   Named owners and due dates
Decisions and next steps   10:35–10:45   Lock decisions and immediate follow-ups   Confirm final decisions; capture action items; set post-meeting follow-up   Final decision log and action list
Agenda Blocks to Use in the Meeting
- Confirm what must be decided by 10:45
- Call out any urgent launch risks
Discussion goal:   Align on outcomes and keep the meeting decision-oriented.
- Separate launch blockers from post-launch issues
- Confirm fix, defer, or monitor for each critical item
Discussion goal:   Leave with a ranked list of bugs and a clear recommendation on what must be fixed before launch.
- Identify where users drop off most
- Discuss likely UX, technical, or messaging causes
Discussion goal:   Agree on the top metric problem to address first and what follow-up analysis or experiment is needed.
- Review readiness across product, design, engineering, and QA
- Surface any gaps in release prep
Discussion goal:   Determine checklist status and identify anything that could delay launch.
- Assign one clear owner per open item
- Avoid shared ownership without a primary accountable person
Discussion goal:   Ensure every priority item has a directly responsible owner and target date.
- Read back action items and deadlines
- Agree on status update channel or next checkpoint
Discussion goal:   End with no ambiguity on decisions, owners, and immediate next moves.
Use this structure during the meeting:
